text: Open your own repo in one step: pnpm dev <path or git url>
description: Zero-setup entry for outside developers: `pnpm dev ~/code/my-repo` (or start) prints a link http://localhost:4000/?project=<abs path> that opens that repo directly and creates its .bowman on first open; a Git URL prints a ?repo= read-only link. Path resolves against the caller's directory (pnpm INIT_CWD). Also: launcher --dry-run no longer writes runtime-config.json (it repointed a running stack's frontend) and validate:local-runtime no longer deletes the live config — it parses the printed dry-run config.

status.comment: Verified: dry-run prints project/repo links, missing dir exits 1; ?project= on an empty folder created .bowman in the running app; validate:local-runtime PASS with live config checksum unchanged; pnpm check 25/25.
